# Retrospective: PR #12834 follow-up

## What worked

- Fresh native sessions and equivalent neutral assignments preserved independence. No historical private deliberations were supplied.
- Both reviewers generated their own private runtime evidence. The original generated shortcut provided a meaningful negative control, and actual producer outputs distinguished refusal from dispatch.
- Inspecting Chromium's complete normalization path exposed whitespace behavior beyond the published prefix/value cases.
- A standard synthetic Desktop Action tested the migration's customization-preservation promise. Post-independence Fable inspection confirmed the source/evidence interpretation without pretending to be an independent rerun.
- Six sealed bundles were reverified by the coordinator. The zero-exit fixture explicitly retained the custom-action preservation failure instead of presenting it as a pass.

## Friction and deviations

- Fable's migration fixture used fixed one-second sleeps for installer background dispatch. This is a readiness-method deviation from the workflow, not a safety breach. Captures are present, but the successful child-dispatch claim relies on Astra's source-and-wait fixture. Preserve Fable's raw evidence and use an explicit wait in future fixtures.
- Coordinator confirmed Herdr's managed environment after its initial reviewer controls rather than before. HERDR_ENV was 1, and controls targeted only owned registered Team 4 reviewer panes. Check this first in future rounds.
- Reviewers differed on whether whitespace is a new observation or continuation of F2, and on its public prominence. The report records the disagreement and the coordinator's bounded rationale; no fabricated consensus or withdrawal.

## Process observations

No confirmed review-tool bug, failed setup, isolation failure, desktop-resource request or Fable exhaustion signal occurred. Six synchronous namespace runs completed; no host process cleanup was needed. Source clones and sealed evidence are retained. No package, service, firewall, browser or real-account experiments ran on the host.

No Omadev slot was allocated or used, so this round provides no new Omadev findings. No changes to tooling or reviewed code were made.

## Carry forward

Test migration authorization predicates against rewrite scope, especially standard multi-group configuration files. Keep source-only browser semantics visibly distinct from executed launcher behavior. Preserve successful original examples even when another normalization gap remains. Generic test recommendations and minor cosmetic notes add no useful public signal here.

HTML is saved only. Publication and next assignment remain the outer assistant's responsibility.
comment:
**Verified:** At `39b0d6b3999e`, the [earlier review's](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12834#issuecomment-5768241141) generated-shortcut issue is resolved and its demonstrated switch spellings are fixed. The broader switch-normalization issue remains in a whitespace form; a new migration issue affects custom desktop actions.

**Verified:** Production-script checks reproduced the author's prefix/value fixes and normal shortcut repair:

| Case | Current result |
| --- | --- |
| Old generated Sunshine command, after migration | Dispatches without the obsolete flag; repeat migration leaves content unchanged |
| Edited main command carrying the flag | Left unchanged with a manual-removal warning |
| `-ignore-certificate-errors`, `--no-sandbox=1` | Refused before dispatch |
| `--ignore-certificate-errors-spki-list=…` | Forwarded as intended |

Browser dispatch was captured, not executed.

## Remaining: whitespace-padded switches escape the guard

`bin/omarchy-launch-webapp:22-27` normalizes the raw argument without trimming it. Quoted single arguments such as `" --ignore-certificate-errors"` and `"--ignore-certificate-errors "` still reach browser dispatch. These forms also passed the previously reviewed revision; the published single-dash and `=value` examples no longer do.

```text
One argument: " --ignore-certificate-errors"
Launcher, executed:              raw prefix check skips it -> forwarded
Chromium POSIX, source-inspected: ASCII trim -> denied switch name
```

Chromium [trims surrounding ASCII whitespace before parsing switches](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/c437277394832d12031fc109ba0a6797dbfccd4c/base/command_line.cc#L643-L674), and its [certificate-error setting checks switch presence](https://github.com/chromium/chromium/blob/c437277394832d12031fc109ba0a6797dbfccd4c/components/network_session_configurator/browser/network_session_configurator.cc#L831-L837).

**Impact:** The preventive guard still forwards valid spellings of a switch it intends to exclude. This requires a caller to supply whitespace inside one argument. No in-tree caller or attacker-driven trigger was identified, and browser-side effects were source-inspected only.

**Suggested change:** Trim Chromium's surrounding ASCII whitespace for validation before the dash check and name comparison, retaining exact-name matching and leaving unrelated dispatch arguments unchanged.

## New: the migration rewrites unrelated desktop-action commands

`migrations/1790062793.sh:19-24` checks the first `Exec=` line, then replaces every `Exec=` line. A synthetic customization of the production-generated shortcut added a standard Documentation action without changing the main command. The migration repaired the main command but also changed the action:

```diff
 [Desktop Action Documentation]
 Name=Documentation
-Exec=omarchy-launch-webapp https://docs.lizardbyte.dev/projects/sunshine/
+Exec=omarchy-launch-webapp https://localhost:47990
```

[Desktop actions have their own `Exec` keys](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry/latest/extra-actions.html#extra-actions-keys); this is not a duplicate key within the main group.

**Impact:** A user-added action loses its intended command and opens the admin page instead. The normal generated shortcut is repaired correctly; this reproduction concerns a customized file, not a discovered affected user's setup.

**Suggested change:** Restrict replacement to the matched generated command in the main `[Desktop Entry]` group, preserving other groups' commands, or warn and leave multi-command customizations untouched.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Production shell scripts with synthetic browser entries and stubbed browser/package/service effects, generated-shortcut replay, private single-migration integration, targeted repository tests, and pinned Chromium source inspection. No live browser TLS, certificate-warning UI, singleton launch order, desktop-action menu, Sunshine service, or complete upgrade was tested.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Fresh Astra coordinator inspection, independent Fable 5.1 High and Astra Xhigh technical reviews, then synthesis against saved evidence and a post-independence check of the custom-action case.
